MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 25, 2023
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Silverstein called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Bruce Silverstein; Mayor Pro Tem Steve Uhring; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Doug Stewart

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey
  Pettij ohn, City Clerk; Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Yolanda Bundy,
  Environmental Sustainability Director; Richard Mollica, Flaming Director; Susan Duenas,
  Public Safety Director; Rob DuBouX, Public Works Director; Jason Lawrence, Deputy City
  Clerk; and Christina Munoz, Deputy City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Jefferson Wagner led the Pledge of Allegiance.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  September 15, 2023, with the amended agenda posted on September 21, 2023.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Councilmember Stewart moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Uhring seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda, hearing Item No. 6.B. after the consent calendar, continuing
  Item No. 7.A. to the October 9, 2023 meeting, and adjourn in memory of Los
  Angeles County Sheriff Deputy Ryan Clinkunbroomer. The question was called,
  and the motion carried unanimously.

ITEM l  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Presentation on First Responder Readiness for Fire Season

  Battalion Chief Joshua Binder, Los Angeles County Fire Department, and Captain
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of September 25, 2023
  Page 2 of 20

  Jennifer Seetoo, Los Angeles County Sheriff s Department, provided a presentation
  on First Responder Readiness for Fire Season.

  B.  City Council Reorganization

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor public comment.

  Speakers: John Mazza and Pamela Conly Ulich

  1.  Presentations to Outgoing Mavor

  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring presented a Wave award to Mayor Silverstein for
  outstanding service and dedication as the mayor of the City of Malibu from
  2022 to 2023.

  Remarks by Outgoing Mayor

  Mayor Silverstein stated that it was a sincere honor and pleasure to serve as
  mayor for the past nine and a half months and he would be pleased to turn
  over the reins to the new mayor.

  Election of Mayor

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to nominations for Mayor.

MOTION  Mayor Silverstein nominated Mayor Pro Tem Uhring for Mayor.

  Mayor Silverstein closed the floor to nominations for Mayor.

  The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

  The meeting was turned over to newly elected Mayor Uhring.

  Election of Mayor Pro Tem

  Mayor Uhring opened the floor to nominations for Mayor Pro Tem.

MOTION  Councilmember Grisanti moved, and Mayor Uhring seconded a motion to
  nominate Councilmember Stewart for Mayor Pro Tem.

  Mayor Uhring closed the floor to nominations for Mayor Pro Tem.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

  Administration of Oath of Office to Newly Elected Mayor and Mayor Pro
  Tem
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of September 25, 2023
  Page 3 of 20

  Marcia Uhring administered the Oath of Office to newly elected Mayor
  Uhring.

  Sharon Stewart administered the Oath of Office to newly elected Mayor Pro
  Tem Stewart.

  6.  Remarks by Newly Elected Mayor

  Mayor Uhring commented that upon moving to Malibu more than 30 years
  prior, long-time resident Ozzie Silna introduced him to the General Plan,
  Mission, and Vision Statements. He expressed appreciation for the late Mr.
  Silna and stated that he tried to follow the tradition set forth by him. He
  stated that it was with a profound sense of responsibility that he accepted
  the honor and privilege to serve as mayor. He expressed gratitude to his
  wife, fellow City Councilmembers, and the people of Malibu for placing
  their trust in him. He stated that he was a firm believer of Malibu’s General
  Plan, Mission, and Vision Statements and that he would continue to fight to
  follow that plan, as he had for over 30 years. He stated that he would
  endeavor to work collaboratively with his fellow Councilmembers and the
  community to ensure a bright and sustainable future for the city. He
  recognized the hard work and dedication of City employees. He thanked
  Malibu again for the incredible honor, and suggested that they embarked on
  this journey together, for a brighter and more prosperous future for the city.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Tim Pera, MRCA, provided the monthly ranger activity report. He reported
  additional rangers addressed the high volume ofVisitors to their parks on weekends.
  He reported 13 administrative citations were issued at La Chuza Beach for dogs on
  the beach and possession of alcohol and three issued at Escondido Canyon Trail for
  illegal offtrail use and for dogs off leash. He reported continuous patrols for illegal
  parking and directed patrols were implemented to prevent injuries in the back
  country. He stated that no homeless encampments were observed at Bluffs Park or
  reported at any of their parks and no service calls were generated. He stated that
  approximately 308 parking citations were issued at the parks and beach accessways,
  and maintenance was conducted throughout the month.

  Kevin Keegan, Parent Teacher Student Association (PTSA) for Malibu Middle and
  High School, discussed the importance of school safety and expressed concern that
  safety and security recommendations from the school safety assessment had not
  been made available. He discussed the history of the School Safety Ad Hoc
  Committee and the school safety assessment conducted by Guidepost Solutions. He
  stated that on May 22, 2023, the Malibu PTSA, their two elementary school Parent
  Teacher Associations (PTA), and School Leadership Council sent a joint letter to
  the City Council School Safety Ad Hoc Committee, requesting the consultant report
  be given priority attention over the summer.

permit.

  discussed progress of Dark Sky Ordinance compliance for gas stations, shopping

  permit in question was an SEP and clarified that TUPs applied to all

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, congratulated

  assignment deputies conducted a traffic stop and determined the driver had two

ITEM 2.C.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Grisanti stated he attended the interfaith breakfast hosted by
  Captain Jennifer Seetoo. He stated that they discussed using the network of
  churches and synagogues to provide another level of protection for emergencies.
  He stated that he attended the League of California Cities Annual Conference in

Sacramento the week prior and hoped interactions with members of the State

County Usage Director Helene Schneider, who was working on homelessness. He
thanked Mr. Ahem for bringing attention to the dim lighting in the Council
Chambers. He stated that he missed the opening of the Dick Van Dyke art exhibit
at City Hall and encouraged the public to Visit the gallery. He commented on the
quality of the exhibits and thanked the Arts Commission.

Councilmember Riggins commented on preparations by the Sheriffs Department
and Fire Department for the upcoming fire season. She discussed the recent
evacuation zone notification test for Point Dume and advised residents who were
not alerted to sign up for emergency notifications. She stated that she attended the
League of California Cities Annual Conference in Sacramento. She congratulated
newly elected Mayor Uhring.

In response to Councilmember Riggins, Mr. Pera stated three MRCA rangers were
typically assigned to the Malibu area and stated there were night and day patrols
throughout the week.

Councilmember Silverstein thanked the public speakers and those who submitted
written comments. He stated that he attended his last California Strategies meeting
and that the new Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem would attend mture meetings. He
stated that he spent much time reviewing the appeal that was scheduled to be heard
tonight night, but was continued. He stated that it was beneficial for the Council to
have the communications received from the public about the ADU discussion from
the prior meeting. In response to Mr. Keegan, he provided an update on school
safety efforts. He stated that he and Councilmember Grisanti were appointed to the
ad hoc committee promptly with the obj ective to have the assessment report before
the 2022-23 school year began but it was delayed by the school district’s slow
deliberate process. He stated that he received a draft report some time ago and
people would be pleased with the good recommendations, but it shod  ul have been
provided sooner. In response to Mr. Ross, he identified recipients of benefits or
questionable discretionary decisions: POOSH, Yves Saint Laurent, Nobu, Steve
Soboroff, and James Perse. He stated that there were billionaires and celebrities
who lived on Point Dume who were identified to him by various residnts,  e  and
those interested in more information could speak to him directly. He stated that
there were numerous wealthy property owners that went before the Flaming
Commission and City Council routinely and more frequently for variances and
questionable projects than average Malibu residents. He requested a consensus
from Council to bring back an item to amend the SEP ordinance to have a
reasonable noticing requirement that informed residents and provided them the
opportunity to obj ect.

Mayor Uhring indicated his  support for  Councilmember  Silverstein’s
recommendation.

Mayor Pro Tem Stewart commented that SEPs for private property were related to
   Malibu City Council

TUPs for commercial properties, and there should be consistency between the two.
He suggested the matters be brought back together. He commented on the
inconsistencies with the TUP process as it pertained to the triathlon.

Interim City Attorney Rusin requested clarification if there was support for the
Council to bring back an option to initiate a zoning text amendment for when the
TUP ordinance comes before the Council.

Mayor Pro Tem Stewart stated that he preferred having both issues brought back
together.

Councilmember Riggins recommended having the issue studied by the Zoning
Ordinance Revisions and Code Enforcement Subcommittee (ZORACES).

Mayor Uhring stated there were discrepancies between the processes TUPs and
SEPs but making them consistent with each other shouldn’t be problematic and he
would prefer having the matter addressed quickly without going through
ZORACES.

Interim City Attorney Rusin stated that if the matter was brought back with the
option for the Council to initiate the amendment, at that point it could be decided if
it went straight to the Planning Commission or ZORACES.

 In response to Mayor Uhring, Councilmember Riggins recommended caution when
 considering amendments. She stated that there were times where individuals
 proposed parties or other events that might be inconsistent with what residents
 wanted, but she also did not want residents to be unduly burdened when trying to
permit their own small events
Commissioner Silverstein stated that he asked for consensus for an item to be
brought back to decide whether an amendment should be proposed. He stated that
they were not supposed to be engaged in discussion about the amendment. He stated
he heard one second to his proposal from Mayor Uhring.

Councilmember Grisanti stated that when Item No. 6.B. was discussed, penalties
for misrepresentation could be discussed and they would get a good sense of
whether SEPs and TUPs should be considered together.

Councilmember Silverstein stated that there would be discussion on the matter
during Item No. 6.B. He stated that he would talk at length about the weekend event,
which was a cautionary tale as to why Item No. 6.B. made sense. He stated that
Item No. 6.B. had to do with what the rule should be, for which there would then
be enforcement. He stated that his proposed item would establish a rule.

Councilmember Grisanti stated that when a person applied for a permit or did not,
and then held an event that was larger than was permitted, or permittable, or
violated their conditional use permit (CUP), that it was appropriate for a much more
   Malibu City Council

serious set of consequences than currently existed.

Councilmember Silverstein clarified that what he proposed had nothing to do with
enforcement. He stated that the current rule, was that there was no pre-notice
requirement for getting an SEP. He stated an applicant could go into the City the
day prior or the day of the event, and it could be granted that day. He stated, by
contrast, a TUP required substantial advance notice so that the public might obj ect,
a considered decision made, and proper safety protocols put into place. He stated
all those elements needed to be established. He stated what he was specifically
talking about was coming back for a decision on whether to amend the provision to
impose certain noticing requirements. He stated that Item No. 6.B. was addressing
penalties for violations.

Mayor Pro Tem Stewart recommended TUP and SEP regulations be brought back
together. He indicated agreement with Commissioner Riggins’ suggestion for the
matter to be addressed in a ZORACES meeting. He stated that he understood from
Interim City Attorney Rusin, that they either assigned it back to Council, the
Planning Commission, or ZORACES.

In response to the Mayor Pro Tem Stewart, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated that
he thought what he was suggesting was to have an item brought back initiating a
zone text amendment (ZTA), to address the notice provisions ofthe SEP ordinance,
while the TUP ordinance was brought forward for consideration by the Council. He
stated that at that point, it could be decided by Council whether to initiate that ZTA,
and if it was wanted for the ZTA to go to ZORACES or go straight to the Flaming
Commission. He stated that he believed he wanted to bring that item forward at the
same time as the TUP ordinance.

Mayor Pro Tem Stewart stated that was correct and there was cleanup that needed
to be done both code sections, and his recommendation was for it.to be done all at
one time.

Councilmember Silverstein stated that he respected everyone’s position, and that
he believed he was in the minority and that it would not come back the way that he
and Mayor Uhring proposed. He stated that he would have much more to say about
the POOSH matter when Item No. 6.B. was heard.

Mayor Pro Tem Stewart commented on the tremendous loss of Los Angeles County
Sheriff Deputy Ryan Clinkunbroomer from the Palmdale station. He stated that the
Sheriff Department and the Volunteers on Patrol (VOP), protected and served the
community every day. He reported that he attended the PCH task force meeting and
discussed jurisdiction of the Zuma Beach underpass and stated that it was not the
City’s, was on Beaches and Harbors’ land, with Caltrans access, and the U.S.
Department of Wildlife Fish and Game said there were tidewater gobies in the water
flooding the underpass. He stated that the City of Malibu was not mentioned except
to say they were concerned about the safety aspects of cars entering and leaving
PCH and the effect it had on the City. He stated that if the City had more control

  they would probably have a better solution for the triathlon. He reported that he
  attended a Las Virgenes-Malibu Council of Governments (COG) meeting. He
  spoke highly ofthe Library Speaker Series and stated that the Beatles’ Sgt. Pepper’s
  Lonely Hearts Club Band event was well attended. He stated that SEP, TUP, and
  STR issuance problems needed to be addressed and emphasized the importance of
  enforcement in obtaining compliance. He stated that there would be a Special City

  The appellant contends that several factors outside oftheir control forced a redesign
  of the intended routes for the event. The factors included severe flooding and the
  creation of an environmentally sensitive area around the Zuma Underpass which
  has impacted their ability to use the proposed racecourse. The racecourse had not.
  been finalized before the deadline for the City to issue the 32-day public notice nor
  was it finalized prior to the 24—day deadline to render a decision, and therefore, the
  Flaming Director denied TUP No. 23-004.

  Based on evidence contained Within the record, including the agenda report, the
  appeal, and the testimony provided at the hearing on September 25, 2023, and
  pursuant to the MMC, the City Council adopts the findings of fact, granting the
  appeal and finds that substantial evidence in the record supports approval of TUP
  No. 23-004. In addition, the analysis, findings of fact, as well as the testimony and
  materials considered by the City Council are incorporated herein as though fully
  set forth.

  A. The City Council finds that notice was provided consistent with MMC
  17.68.050, which requires a five-day public notice of the event. The applicant
  provided mailed written notice consistent with MMC section 17.68.050 on or about
  September 20, 2023. This event has also been consistently advertised and proposed
  for this date and this apprOximate location (the same general location it has been
  held in during this same period of time for many years). This event has received
  substantial attention from the public and the date and approximate location is well
  known to the community.

  B. The City Council makes the findings for approval as more fully detailed
  in attachment A (permit).
